I realize I need to fix the missing sys.path insertion and properly reload the module, plus make sure the combined kernel includes primary electron contributions, not just secondary production. I should set up the imports and kernel definition correctly in one consolidated call, with the kernel normalized as energy deposited per unit mass per production event.

Working through the convolution math, I need to normalize the raw kernel so it sums to one (fraction of energy per depth bin), then convolve this with the total energy-transfer density at each depth to get the dose profile—being careful about units since the energy-transfer term is per unit mass while the kernel needs to map correctly onto depth bins.

These production weights are relative per-volume values, so normalization isn't critical since only ratios matter in the kernel. Each source electron's energy T gets deposited in full, with the weight-times-energy implicitly tracking the total deposited energy.

import sys, pickle; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/work')
import numpy as np, importlib
import mcana, mcmod, ana as A, pdd as P, final as F, kern as K
from mcana import *
from mcmod import *
tal=pickle.load(open('/tmp/work/tal_run1.pkl','rb'))
rng=np.random.default_rng(7)
ptal,Pper=A.primary_electron_tally(rng, Ns=400000)
nh=tal['nh']
Cnc = tal['q_fine_all_cos']/nh + ptal['q_fine_all_cos']
dF = FINE[1:]-FINE[:-1]; cF=np.sqrt(FINE[:-1]*FINE[1:])
xg, kr, tot = K.kernel_from_sources(Cnc, cF, dF, zbin=0.1, xmin=-2.0, xmax=12.0, ns=400)
kn = kr*0.1/ (kr*0.1).sum()     # fraction per 0.1 cm bin
print("kernel total", (kr*0.1).sum(), "mean depth", np.sum(kn*(xg[:-1]+0.05)))
# depth-dose
zm,Ktot,Ks,Kp = P.depth_profiles(tal, nh)
zgrid = np.arange(0,10,0.1)+0.05   # bins 0.1 wide
Kz = Ktot   # per bin 0..10 (100 bins)
# convolution D(z_i) = sum_j K(z_j) * kn[(i-j)] where kn index mapping x=z_i-z_j
xc = xg[:-1]+0.05
D = np.zeros(100)
for i in range(100):
    s=0.0
    for j in range(100):
        xk = zm[i]-zm[j]
        k_idx = int(np.floor((xk - xg[0])/0.1))
        if 0<=k_idx<len(kn): s+=Kz[j]*kn[k_idx]
    D[i]=s
imax=np.argmax(D)
print("dmax approx", zm[imax], "D(5)/Dmax*100", 100*D[np.argmin(np.abs(zm-5))]/D.max())
print(np.round(D[:12]/D.max(),3))
"}
